title: Claude Code — check what stuck
intro: Nine self-check questions written from the course notes (no official quiz exists).

choices: Scans the codebase and writes CLAUDE.md — auto-loaded project memory covering commands, architecture, and style
questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md is the project's standing memory, included in context every launch — and it's a draft: the course immediately corrects it with # (uv usage, DB schemas).

questions.prompt: You notice Claude repeating the same mistake (using pip in a uv project). The right move is…
choices: # to add a memory the moment the error repeats
questions.explanation: # appends a permanent memory to CLAUDE.md in one keystroke. Clearing the conversation doesn't fix a knowledge gap — teaching does.

choices: /clear wipes history (between unrelated tasks); /compact summarizes it in place (mid-task, bloated context)
questions.explanation: Context is a budget: wipe it between tasks, compress it within one. ESC interrupts mid-flight; double-ESC rewinds.

questions.prompt: The strongest feature prompts in the course contain…
choices: @-anchored files, current AND desired behavior, and explicit constraints
Only the desired behavior — context wastes tokens
A request to 'make it better' plus a deadline
questions.explanation: The clickable-citations prompt names the files, states where links already live, defines the target behavior, and constrains the result (invisible embeds, matching styles).

questions.prompt: The Playwright MCP server is attached so that…
choices: Claude can write Playwright tests only
Claude can visit the running app, take screenshots, and verify visual work itself
questions.explanation: Visual follow-ups become verifiable: 'visit 127.0.0.1:8000, view the button, make it match.' /permissions can allow the screenshot tool by its full name.

questions.prompt: Lesson 4's debugging prompt asks for tests at three layers because…
choices: More tests always means better code
Layered tests make the failure localize itself before any fix is proposed
Single tests are not allowed in pytest
It's faster than reading the config
questions.explanation: Tool, generator, and end-to-end tests triangulate: two layers pass honestly, one shows the anomaly — leading straight to MAX_RESULTS = 0. Evidence before surgery.

choices: Clone the repo three times with different remotes
Check out multiple branches of the same repo into separate directories — isolated files, shared history — one Claude session per feature
questions.explanation: Three independent features (UI, tests, quality) proceed in parallel; the merge back — delegated to Claude — is the only serial step. Start from a clean tree.

questions.prompt: A hook differs from a custom slash command because…
choices: A hook fires deterministically at lifecycle points (before/after tools, on finish); a slash command is a packaged prompt you trigger
questions.explanation: Commands package prompts ($ARGUMENTS for the variable part) and can drift like any instruction; hooks are shell commands the lifecycle guarantees.

questions.prompt: In the Figma lesson, two MCP servers are attached because…
choices: One is a backup for the other
One reads the source of truth (the mockup); the other verifies the built app against it (Playwright)
questions.explanation: Claude both builds and checks — against artifacts, not adjectives. The follow-up wires real FRED data into the finished dashboard.
